tiers.client-only: All state and logic in one browser; no server state, sign-in or push. Local persistence (browser storage) only if resuming is asked for.
tiers.client-plus-light-server: Game or tool runs in the client; a small server endpoint holds only the shared or trusted part (for example validated scores).
tiers.server-shared-async: Authoritative shared state on the server with runtime identity; other parties learn of changes on their next visit or by notification (email, platform notification); no live channel.
tiers.server-shared-live: Authoritative shared state on the server with runtime identity and a live or near-live channel (short poll, SSE, WebSocket or platform push) justified by the latency the request states.
tiers.server-batch: Scheduled or triggered server work with no interactive client in the loop; idempotent, retried, observable.
tiers.server-public: Server state reachable by anonymous or untrusted callers; abuse controls and validation are central.
tiers.host-scoped: State lives with one host record or document (document properties, the host record's related data) and follows the host's own sharing; no separate database or access model.

scenarios.name: solo-inline-game
scenarios.request: Build a Battleship game that one person plays in the browser against the computer.
scenarios.overbuild: Server-held game state, sign-in, a database or a push channel for this request is overbuilt; hiding the computer's fleet from its only player protects nothing.

scenarios.name: hotseat-game
scenarios.request: Build a checkers game two people play by taking turns on the same computer.
scenarios.overbuild: Accounts, server state or a sync channel are overbuilt for two people sharing one screen.

scenarios.name: solo-game-with-leaderboard
scenarios.request: Build a single-player minesweeper game in the browser with a shared leaderboard of the best times, visible to everyone who plays.
scenarios.overbuild: Running the whole game on the server is overbuilt; the leaderboard entry is the shared, trusted part. A plausibility check or an explicit accepted-risk decision on submitted times is expected.

scenarios.name: async-turn-multiplayer
scenarios.request: Build correspondence chess for colleagues: two people start a game and each makes a move whenever they get to it, often a day apart. Each player is told when it is their turn.
scenarios.overbuild: A WebSocket or streaming channel is overbuilt for moves a day apart; notification on turn change is the requirement.

scenarios.name: live-multiplayer
scenarios.request: Build live multiplayer Battleship: two signed-in people play in real time and each sees the other's shot within a second or two.
scenarios.overbuild: None expected beyond the live channel; the channel must be justified by the stated latency.

scenarios.name: team-task-board
scenarios.request: Build a task board for a team of about 20 colleagues: create, assign, move and comment on tasks. Changes by others should appear without a manual reload within a minute.
scenarios.overbuild: A minute of freshness does not need WebSockets where polling fits the quota; a new database is overbuilt where the runtime has native records.

scenarios.name: approval-workflow
scenarios.request: Build an expense request flow: an employee submits an amount and receipt link, their manager approves or rejects, the employee is emailed the outcome, and finance can see an audit trail.
scenarios.overbuild: A custom approval engine is overbuilt where the runtime offers approvals or workflow automation.

scenarios.name: read-heavy-dashboard
scenarios.request: Build a dashboard showing sales KPIs computed from about 50,000 existing order rows, viewed by around 100 people a day. Figures may be up to 15 minutes old.
scenarios.overbuild: A write path, a new data store or a live channel is overbuilt; a native cache or precomputed summary sized to the 15-minute freshness is expected.

scenarios.name: scheduled-external-sync
scenarios.request: Every night, pull the previous day's orders from a partner's REST API (needs an API key, rate-limited to 60 requests a minute) and store them so reports can use them.
scenarios.overbuild: A client UI or live channel is overbuilt; idempotent upserts, retry, rate-limit handling, secret custody and failure visibility are the requirement.

scenarios.name: public-feedback-form
scenarios.request: Build a public feedback form anyone can submit without an account (name optional, email optional, message required), protected from spam, with a page where our staff read and resolve submissions.
scenarios.overbuild: Accounts for submitters are overbuilt; abuse controls and staff-only access are the requirement.

scenarios.name: file-upload-processing
scenarios.request: Let employees upload photos of receipts; extract the total and date from each and show the employee the result when it is ready.
scenarios.overbuild: A custom file server is overbuilt where the runtime stores files natively.

scenarios.name: team-chat
scenarios.request: Build a simple team chat room: signed-in members post messages, see new messages within a few seconds, and can scroll back through history.
scenarios.overbuild: Presence, typing indicators or reactions were not requested.

scenarios.name: offline-field-checklist
scenarios.request: Field inspectors fill in a site checklist on their phones, often with no signal; answers must reach the office once they are back online, without losing or duplicating any.
scenarios.overbuild: Real-time sync is overbuilt; a durable local queue with idempotent upload and conflict rule is the requirement.

scenarios.name: llm-summarizer
scenarios.request: Add a button that summarizes the current document with an external AI API and shows the summary to the person who asked.
scenarios.overbuild: Storing every summary permanently or a shared database is overbuilt unless reuse is asked; the API key must never reach the client.

scenarios.name: docs-sidebar-addon
scenarios.request: Add a sidebar to a Google Doc where the author tags sections with a status; the tags stay with that document and anyone who can edit the document sees them.
scenarios.overbuild: A spreadsheet or external database, or a custom access list, is overbuilt; the document's own properties and sharing are the home and the authority.

scenarios.name: record-page-panel
scenarios.request: On the Account record page, show a panel with the account's open cases and let support agents add a quick note to a case.
scenarios.overbuild: A custom object for notes or custom sharing logic is overbuilt where standard objects and the org's sharing already apply; the user's record access is the authority.

scenarios.name: multi-tenant-booking
scenarios.request: Build a small appointment-booking service where each business signs up, invites its staff and manages its own calendar; customers book slots by link. Businesses must never see each other's data.
scenarios.overbuild: Per-tenant infrastructure is overbuilt for a small service; tenant scoping enforced on every server query, with a negative test, is the requirement.

scenarios.name: capacity-registration
scenarios.request: Build an event registration page with 200 seats: people sign in with a Google account to register, and the event must never be oversold, even when registration opens and hundreds try at once.
scenarios.overbuild: A queue or live channel is overbuilt if an atomic conditional write enforces the seat count; a load or concurrency test is expected.

scenarios.name: payment-webhook
scenarios.request: Receive payment-succeeded webhooks from our payment provider and mark the matching order as paid. The same webhook can arrive twice or out of order.
scenarios.overbuild: A client UI or live channel is overbuilt; signature verification, idempotent processing keyed by event ID, and ordering rules are the requirement.
